summary: Contestants demonstrate foundational knowledge of computer programming concepts through an objective test. The event covers languages, logic, algorithm design, data structures, and core software development principles.
time_limits: no more than sixty (60) minutes testing time
what_to_bring: (Optional) Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards. See NLC Calculator Guidelines.
competencies: Demonstrate foundational understanding of computer science principles, including logic, data structures, and algorithms, and demonstrate proficiency in modern programming languages with adaptability to others as needed
Design and implement efficient algorithms using structured and object-oriented design techniques to create scalable and maintainable software solutions
Develop applications using control flow, logical operations, strings, arrays, classes, file I/O, loops, and advanced data structures to process and manage data effectively
Apply the software development lifecycle and create design artifacts such as UML diagrams, flowcharts, and pseudocode to plan, implement, and communicate system architecture
Write and optimize SQL queries to interact with relational databases for data storage, retrieval, and analysis
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Reference materials are not allowed. Contestants who violate this rule will be disqualified
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this objective event.
